about: Each bill-catalog policy question has one spoken name in two fixed forms, so a stand can be said as a plain sentence: `about` is a noun phrase that reads after 'about' or 'on' ('the bill is about a higher minimum wage'); `to` is a verb phrase that reads after 'to' or 'I want to' ('I want to raise the minimum wage'). Authored to the English engine's patterns, American English; a question with no entry is not offered as a stand. Each question also has a form for each side, written by scripts/words/question-sides.ts: `for` is what a supporter wants done and `against` what an opponent will keep off the books ("keep higher tariffs off the books"), and `repeal` what they will undo; both read after "I want to" and "I will". `today` says how the question stands now, as each side describes it: `without.for` and `without.against` while no law answers it yes, `with.for` and `with.against` once one does. `family` and `pole` type the belief a speaker gives (speech-outline.ts); `number` is `one` or `many`, for the verbs that agree with `about`; `figures` names the measures that bear on the question and the side each helps.
author: Claude Code, pool session

us-policy-positions:transportation-infra.to: make public transit free to ride
us-policy-positions:transportation-infra.for: make public transit free to ride
us-policy-positions:transportation-infra.against: keep free fares on public transit off the books

without.for: Every rider pays a fare to get on the bus or the train, and for a lot of folks that fare adds up fast.
without.against: The folks who ride the bus and the train pay a fare toward what it costs to run them.

with.for: Nobody pays a fare to ride the bus or the train, so getting to work costs a family nothing.
with.against: Nobody who rides the bus pays a fare, so every taxpayer covers the whole cost of running it.

us-policy-positions:transportation-infra.repeal: repeal free fares on public transit
us-policy-positions:transportation-infra.keep: keep free fares on public transit on the books

us-policy-positions:transportation-infra.about: a mileage fee in place of the fuel tax
us-policy-positions:transportation-infra.to: replace the fuel tax with a mileage fee
us-policy-positions:transportation-infra.for: replace the fuel tax with a mileage fee
us-policy-positions:transportation-infra.against: keep a mileage fee in place of the fuel tax off the books

without.for: Roads are paid for by a tax on gas, and drivers of electric cars pay almost nothing toward them.
without.against: Drivers pay for the roads at the pump, and nobody has to keep track of how far they drive.

with.for: Drivers pay for the roads by the mile they drive, so everyone who uses them pays a share.
with.against: Drivers pay the state for every mile they drive, and the state keeps count of where their cars go.

us-policy-positions:transportation-infra.repeal: repeal a mileage fee in place of the fuel tax
us-policy-positions:transportation-infra.keep: keep a mileage fee in place of the fuel tax on the books

us-policy-positions:transportation-infra.against: keep public broadband off the books

without.for: Whole neighborhoods can only get internet from one company, at whatever price it sets.
without.against: Companies build the internet lines and compete to bring them to new homes.

with.for: A public network brings internet to homes the companies passed by.
with.against: The government runs an internet network in competition with the companies that pay taxes here.

us-policy-positions:transportation-infra.keep: keep public broadband on the books

us-policy-positions:transportation-infra.against: keep shifting highway money to transit off the books

without.for: Nearly all of our road money goes to highways, and the buses get what's left.
without.against: The money drivers pay at the pump goes to the roads they drive on.

with.for: Part of our highway money goes to buses and trains, and more people have a way to get to work.
with.against: Part of the money drivers pay for roads goes to buses and trains, while the roads wear down.

us-policy-positions:transportation-infra.repeal: repeal shifting highway money to transit
us-policy-positions:transportation-infra.keep: keep shifting highway money to transit on the books

us-policy-positions:health-human-service.against: keep expanding Medicaid off the books

without.for: A worker can earn too much to get Medicaid and still too little to buy insurance.
without.against: Medicaid is kept for the poorest families, the people it was built to serve.

with.for: Working people who earn too little to buy insurance can get Medicaid.
with.against: Medicaid covers far more people than it was built for, and the bill keeps growing.

us-policy-positions:health-human-service.keep: keep expanding Medicaid on the books

us-policy-positions:health-human-service.against: keep a work requirement for Medicaid off the books

without.for: A grown adult who can work can get Medicaid without working.
without.against: An adult on Medicaid can keep seeing a doctor without filling out work papers every month.

with.for: An adult who can work has to work, train or volunteer to keep Medicaid.
with.against: An adult can lose Medicaid over a missed form, even while they're looking for work.

us-policy-positions:health-human-service.repeal: repeal a work requirement for Medicaid
us-policy-positions:health-human-service.keep: keep a work requirement for Medicaid on the books

us-policy-positions:health-human-service.against: keep a work requirement for assistance off the books

without.for: Cash assistance doesn't ask anything of the adults who can work.
without.against: A family that falls on hard times can get cash help without jumping through hoops.

with.for: An adult who can work has to look for work to get cash assistance.
with.against: A family in a hard stretch can lose its help over paperwork about a job search.

us-policy-positions:health-human-service.repeal: repeal a work requirement for assistance
us-policy-positions:health-human-service.keep: keep a work requirement for assistance on the books

us-policy-positions:education.universal-.against: keep universal preschool off the books

without.for: Preschool is something a family pays for or does without.
without.against: Families pick the preschool that suits them, or keep their little ones at home.

with.for: Every four-year-old can go to preschool.
with.against: Every taxpayer pays for preschool, whether a family wants it or not.

us-policy-positions:education.universal-.keep: keep universal preschool on the books

us-policy-positions:education.public-fun.to: pay for private schooling with public money
us-policy-positions:education.public-fun.for: pay for private schooling with public money
us-policy-positions:education.public-fun.against: keep public money for private schools off the books

without.for: A family that picks a private school pays for it twice, in tuition and in taxes.
without.against: Public money stays in the public schools that most of our children attend.

with.for: Public money follows a child to whatever school the family picks.
with.against: Money is pulled out of the public schools that most of our children attend.

us-policy-positions:education.public-fun.repeal: repeal public money for private schools
us-policy-positions:education.public-fun.keep: keep public money for private schools on the books

us-policy-positions:education.raise-teac.about: a higher minimum salary for teachers
us-policy-positions:education.raise-teac.against: keep a higher minimum salary for teachers off the books

without.for: A starting teacher can earn less than a manager at the store down the road.
without.against: Each school district decides what it pays its teachers.

with.for: The law sets a floor under what a teacher is paid.
with.against: The state tells every district what it must pay, whatever its budget holds.

us-policy-positions:education.raise-teac.repeal: repeal a higher minimum salary for teachers
us-policy-positions:education.raise-teac.keep: keep a higher minimum salary for teachers on the books

us-policy-positions:fiscal.adopt-income-.against: keep an income tax off the books

without.for: There is no income tax here, so the sales tax hits working families hardest.
without.against: There is no tax on what people earn here.

with.for: People here pay a tax on what they earn, and it helps keep the sales tax down.
with.against: People here hand over part of every paycheck in income tax.

us-policy-positions:fiscal.adopt-income-.keep: keep an income tax on the books

us-policy-positions:fiscal.cap-property-.about: a cap on property tax growth
us-policy-positions:fiscal.cap-property-.to: cap how fast property taxes can grow
us-policy-positions:fiscal.cap-property-.for: cap how fast property taxes can grow
us-policy-positions:fiscal.cap-property-.against: keep a cap on property tax growth off the books

without.for: A family's property tax can climb as fast as the assessor says.
without.against: The property tax on a family's home is set by the people who count on that money, the schools and the towns.

with.for: The law limits how fast property taxes can rise, and families can plan for it.
with.against: The law caps the property tax, and schools and towns have less to work with.

us-policy-positions:fiscal.cap-property-.repeal: repeal a cap on property tax growth
us-policy-positions:fiscal.cap-property-.keep: keep a cap on property tax growth on the books

us-policy-positions:fiscal.exempt-grocer.about: taking the sales tax off groceries
us-policy-positions:fiscal.exempt-grocer.to: exempt groceries from the sales tax
us-policy-positions:fiscal.exempt-grocer.for: exempt groceries from the sales tax
us-policy-positions:fiscal.exempt-grocer.against: keep taking the sales tax off groceries off the books

without.for: A family pays sales tax on every loaf of bread and gallon of milk.
without.against: The sales tax on food helps pay for schools and roads, and everybody chips in.

with.for: Groceries carry no sales tax, so a family keeps more at the checkout.
with.against: Groceries carry no sales tax, and the money has to come from somewhere else.

us-policy-positions:fiscal.exempt-grocer.repeal: repeal taking the sales tax off groceries
us-policy-positions:fiscal.exempt-grocer.keep: keep taking the sales tax off groceries on the books

us-policy-positions:fiscal.graduated-inc.to: tax higher incomes at higher rates
us-policy-positions:fiscal.graduated-inc.for: tax higher incomes at higher rates
us-policy-positions:fiscal.graduated-inc.against: keep a graduated income tax off the books

without.for: A cook and a company owner pay the same income tax rate.
without.against: Everybody here pays the same income tax rate, and nobody is taxed more for doing well.

with.for: Higher incomes pay a higher rate.
with.against: Folks who earn more pay a higher rate the more they succeed.

us-policy-positions:fiscal.graduated-inc.keep: keep a graduated income tax on the books

us-policy-positions:fiscal.balanced-oper.against: keep a balanced operating budget off the books

without.for: Nothing stops the budget from spending more than comes in.
without.against: The budget can borrow in a hard year to keep schools and services open.

with.for: The law says the budget has to balance every year.
with.against: The law makes the budget balance every year, even when a bad year means cutting services people count on.

us-policy-positions:fiscal.balanced-oper.keep: keep a balanced operating budget on the books

us-policy-positions:fiscal.fund-pensions.against: keep funding pensions on schedule off the books

without.for: The pension fund can be shorted whenever the budget gets tight.
without.against: The pension payment can wait a year when the budget is tight and other needs come first.

with.for: The law says the pension fund gets its full payment on schedule.
with.against: The pension payment comes off the top, before schools and roads see a dollar.

us-policy-positions:fiscal.fund-pensions.keep: keep funding pensions on schedule on the books

us-policy-positions:fiscal.minimum-reser.against: keep a minimum reserve balance off the books

without.for: Nothing makes us keep money aside for a bad year.
without.against: The money that comes in goes to work for people the year it comes in.

with.for: The law makes us keep money aside for a bad year.
with.against: The law locks money away in a reserve while needs go unmet.

us-policy-positions:fiscal.minimum-reser.keep: keep a minimum reserve balance on the books

us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.all.against: keep apartments in single-family neighborhoods off the books

without.for: Most of our land is zoned so that nothing but a single house can go up on it, and rents keep climbing.
without.against: The neighborhoods people bought into are zoned for the single homes they chose.

with.for: Apartments can go up in neighborhoods that once allowed only single houses, and more families can find a place.
with.against: Apartment buildings can go up next door to families who bought in a neighborhood of single homes.

us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.all.keep: keep apartments in single-family neighborhoods on the books

us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.inc.about: an affordable-housing requirement for new buildings
us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.inc.to: require affordable units in new buildings
us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.inc.for: require affordable units in new buildings
us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.inc.against: keep an affordable-housing requirement for new buildings off the books

without.for: A new apartment building can go up without a single unit a working family can afford.
without.against: A builder decides what to build and what to charge for it.

with.for: New buildings have to set aside units a working family can afford.
with.against: Every new building has to rent some units at a loss, and fewer get built.

us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.inc.repeal: repeal an affordable-housing requirement for new buildings
us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.inc.keep: keep an affordable-housing requirement for new buildings on the books

us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.ren.to: limit how much rents can rise
us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.ren.for: limit how much rents can rise
us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.ren.against: keep rent stabilization off the books

without.for: A landlord can raise the rent as much as they like when the lease runs out.
without.against: Rents are set between landlords and tenants, and builders keep building.

with.for: The law limits how much the rent can go up each year.
with.against: The state tells landlords what they can charge, and fewer new homes get built.

us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.ren.keep: keep rent stabilization on the books

us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.rig.about: a lawyer for tenants facing eviction
us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.rig.to: guarantee tenants a lawyer in eviction cases
us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.rig.for: guarantee tenants a lawyer in eviction cases
us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.rig.against: keep a lawyer for tenants facing eviction off the books

without.for: Most tenants face an eviction in court without a lawyer.
without.against: An eviction case is settled between a landlord and a tenant, as it always has been.

with.for: A tenant facing eviction gets a lawyer.
with.against: Taxpayers pay for a lawyer to fight every eviction, and landlords wait months to be paid.

us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.rig.repeal: repeal a lawyer for tenants facing eviction
us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.rig.keep: keep a lawyer for tenants facing eviction on the books

us-federal-positions:labor-commerce.rais.against: keep a higher federal minimum wage off the books

without.for: The federal minimum wage has not gone up in years, while everything else has.
without.against: Each state sets a minimum wage above the federal one when it chooses to, and small businesses can still afford to hire.

with.for: The federal minimum wage is higher than it was, and full-time work pays more.
with.against: The federal minimum wage is higher than it was, and some of the first jobs young people take are gone.

us-federal-positions:labor-commerce.rais.repeal: repeal a higher federal minimum wage
us-federal-positions:labor-commerce.rais.keep: keep a higher federal minimum wage on the books

us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.loca.about: letting cities set their own minimum wage
us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.loca.to: let cities set their own minimum wage
us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.loca.for: let cities set their own minimum wage
us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.loca.against: keep letting cities set their own minimum wage off the books

without.for: A city can't set a minimum wage of its own, whatever living there costs.
without.against: The minimum wage is the same in every town in the state, so a business knows the rules wherever it opens.

with.for: A city can set its own minimum wage to fit what living there costs.
with.against: A business has to keep track of a different minimum wage in every town.

us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.loca.repeal: repeal letting cities set their own minimum wage
us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.loca.keep: keep letting cities set their own minimum wage on the books

us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.rais.against: keep a higher minimum wage off the books

without.for: Someone working full time at the minimum wage still can't cover rent.
without.against: The minimum wage leaves room for small businesses to hire young people and give them a start.

with.for: The minimum wage is higher than it was, and full-time work pays more.
with.against: The minimum wage is higher than it was, and some small businesses are hiring fewer people.

us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.rais.keep: keep a higher minimum wage on the books

us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.paid.against: keep paid family leave off the books

without.for: A worker who stays home with a new baby or a sick parent can lose a paycheck.
without.against: Employers and workers work out time off between them, and a small business isn't handed a new mandate.

with.for: A worker can take paid leave for a new baby or a sick parent.
with.against: Every paycheck pays into a leave program, and small businesses have to cover for the time off.

us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.paid.keep: keep paid family leave on the books

us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.publ.against: keep collective bargaining for public workers off the books

without.for: Public workers can't bargain together over their pay.
without.against: The people's elected officials decide what public workers are paid.

with.for: Public workers can bargain together over their pay.
with.against: Union contracts decide much of what the public payroll costs, and taxpayers pay the bill.

us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.publ.repeal: repeal collective bargaining for public workers
us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.publ.keep: keep collective bargaining for public workers on the books

us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.ban-.about: asking about criminal records on state job applications
us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.ban-.to: bar state agencies from asking about criminal records on job applications
us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.ban-.for: bar state agencies from asking about criminal records on job applications
us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.ban-.against: keep asking about criminal records on state job applications off the books

without.for: A state job application can rule someone out over an old record before they get a hearing.
without.against: A state job application asks about a criminal record up front, so the state knows who it's hiring.

with.for: A state job application doesn't ask about a criminal record up front, so people who served their time get a fair look.
with.against: A state job application doesn't ask about a criminal record up front, and the state finds out late.

us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.ban-.repeal: repeal asking about criminal records on state job applications
us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.ban-.keep: keep asking about criminal records on state job applications on the books

us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.righ.against: keep right-to-work rules off the books

without.for: A worker in a union shop can be made to pay union dues.
without.against: Everybody who gets the raise the union won pays a share of what it costs to win it.

with.for: No worker can be made to pay union dues to keep a job.
with.against: A worker can take the raise the union won without paying a dime toward it.

us-policy-positions:business-commerce.le.against: keep legal cannabis sales off the books

without.against: Selling cannabis is against the law, as it has been.

with.for: Cannabis is sold legally, in licensed stores, and the money is taxed.
with.against: Cannabis is sold in stores up and down the street.

us-policy-positions:business-commerce.le.keep: keep legal cannabis sales on the books

us-policy-positions:business-commerce.ca.about: a cap on consumer loan rates
us-policy-positions:business-commerce.ca.to: cap interest rates on consumer loans
us-policy-positions:business-commerce.ca.for: cap interest rates on consumer loans
us-policy-positions:business-commerce.ca.against: keep a cap on consumer loan rates off the books

without.for: A payday lender can charge hundreds of percent a year on a small loan.
without.against: A family that needs cash fast can still find a lender willing to make the loan.

with.for: The law caps the interest on a consumer loan.
with.against: The law caps loan interest, and families with poor credit can't find anyone who will lend to them.

us-policy-positions:business-commerce.ca.repeal: repeal a cap on consumer loan rates
us-policy-positions:business-commerce.ca.keep: keep a cap on consumer loan rates on the books

us-policy-positions:environment-energy.b.against: keep banning new gas hookups off the books

without.for: New buildings are still hooked up to gas.
without.against: A family building a home can choose gas for the stove and the furnace.

with.for: New buildings are built without gas hookups.
with.against: A family building a home can't choose gas, even where it's the cheapest heat.

us-policy-positions:environment-energy.b.keep: keep banning new gas hookups on the books

us-policy-positions:environment-energy.a.about: letting customers pick their electricity supplier
us-policy-positions:environment-energy.a.to: let customers pick their electricity supplier
us-policy-positions:environment-energy.a.for: let customers pick their electricity supplier
us-policy-positions:environment-energy.a.against: keep letting customers pick their electricity supplier off the books

without.against: One utility answers for keeping the lights on, and it has to answer to the state.

with.for: A family can pick who supplies its electricity.
with.against: Companies sell power door to door, and some families end up paying more than they did.

us-policy-positions:environment-energy.a.repeal: repeal letting customers pick their electricity supplier
us-policy-positions:environment-energy.a.keep: keep letting customers pick their electricity supplier on the books

us-policy-positions:environment-energy.c.to: require utilities to supply clean electricity
us-policy-positions:environment-energy.c.for: require utilities to supply clean electricity
us-policy-positions:environment-energy.c.against: keep a clean electricity standard off the books

without.for: Utilities can burn whatever is cheapest to make our power.
without.against: Utilities make our power from whatever keeps the bills lowest.

with.for: Utilities have to make a growing share of our power clean.
with.against: Utilities have to buy power by the state's formula, and families pay for it on every bill.

us-policy-positions:environment-energy.c.keep: keep a clean electricity standard on the books

us-policy-positions:environment-energy.c.about: a clean air plan for polluted counties
us-policy-positions:environment-energy.c.to: require a clean air plan in polluted counties
us-policy-positions:environment-energy.c.for: require a clean air plan in polluted counties
us-policy-positions:environment-energy.c.against: keep a clean air plan for polluted counties off the books

without.against: Each county answers for its own air without new orders from the state.

with.for: A county with dirty air has to have a plan to clean it.
with.against: Counties answer to the state for every plant and every road, and the costs land on the businesses there.

us-policy-positions:environment-energy.c.repeal: repeal a clean air plan for polluted counties

without.against: A family recycles at the curb, with no deposit added at the store.

with.against: Every bottle and can at the store costs a family a few cents more.

us-policy-positions:environment-energy.b.keep: keep a bottle deposit on the books

us-policy-positions:environment-energy.p.against: keep a price on carbon off the books

without.for: A company can put carbon into the air without paying a cent for it.
without.against: There is no charge on carbon, so power and gas cost what they cost.

with.for: A company pays for the carbon it puts into the air.
with.against: A charge on carbon is added to the price of power and gas, and families pay it.

us-policy-positions:environment-energy.p.keep: keep a price on carbon on the books

us-policy-positions:justice-public-safet.to: give civilians oversight of the police
us-policy-positions:justice-public-safet.for: give civilians oversight of the police
us-policy-positions:justice-public-safet.against: keep civilian oversight of the police off the books

us-policy-positions:justice-public-safet.for: require a permit to carry a concealed gun
us-policy-positions:justice-public-safet.against: keep a permit to carry a concealed gun off the books

without.for: A person can carry a hidden gun without a permit.
without.against: A law-abiding adult can carry a gun to protect themselves without asking for a permit.

with.for: Carrying a hidden gun takes a permit.
with.against: A law-abiding adult has to ask permission to carry a gun for protection.

us-policy-positions:justice-public-safet.repeal: repeal a permit to carry a concealed gun
us-policy-positions:justice-public-safet.keep: keep a permit to carry a concealed gun on the books

us-policy-positions:justice-public-safet.about: a higher age to buy a handgun
us-policy-positions:justice-public-safet.to: raise the age to buy a handgun
us-policy-positions:justice-public-safet.for: raise the age to buy a handgun
us-policy-positions:justice-public-safet.against: keep a higher age to buy a handgun off the books

without.for: An eighteen-year-old can buy a handgun.
without.against: An adult of eighteen can buy a handgun to protect themselves.

with.for: A person has to be older to buy a handgun.
with.against: A grown adult of eighteen can't buy a handgun to protect themselves.

us-policy-positions:justice-public-safet.repeal: repeal a higher age to buy a handgun
us-policy-positions:justice-public-safet.keep: keep a higher age to buy a handgun on the books

us-policy-positions:justice-public-safet.to: remove the duty to retreat before using force
us-policy-positions:justice-public-safet.for: remove the duty to retreat before using force
us-policy-positions:justice-public-safet.against: keep stand-your-ground rules off the books

without.for: A person attacked outside their home has a duty to retreat if they safely can.
without.against: A person attacked outside their home is expected to walk away if they safely can, and fewer arguments end with a gun.

with.for: A person attacked anywhere they have a right to be can stand their ground.
with.against: A person can shoot first in a fight they could have walked away from.

us-policy-positions:justice-public-safet.keep: keep stand-your-ground rules on the books

us-policy-positions:government-operation.to: send every voter a mail ballot
us-policy-positions:government-operation.for: send every voter a mail ballot
us-policy-positions:government-operation.against: keep voting by mail for everyone off the books

without.for: Most voters have to go to a polling place or ask for a ballot by mail.
without.against: Voters come to a polling place, where workers check who they are.

with.for: Every voter gets a ballot in the mail.
with.against: Ballots go out in the mail to every name on the rolls, whether or not that person still lives there.

us-policy-positions:government-operation.repeal: repeal voting by mail for everyone
us-policy-positions:government-operation.keep: keep voting by mail for everyone on the books

us-policy-positions:government-operation.against: keep automatic voter registration off the books

without.for: A citizen has to sign up to vote before they can.
without.against: A citizen signs up to vote when they choose to.

with.for: A citizen is registered to vote automatically.
with.against: People are put on the voter rolls whether they asked to be or not.

us-policy-positions:government-operation.keep: keep automatic voter registration on the books

us-policy-positions:government-operation.to: draw district lines with an independent commission
us-policy-positions:government-operation.for: draw district lines with an independent commission
us-policy-positions:government-operation.against: keep independent redistricting off the books

without.for: The politicians draw their own district lines.
without.against: The lines are drawn by the people the voters elected.

with.for: An independent commission draws the district lines.
with.against: The lines are drawn by a commission no voter ever elected.

us-policy-positions:government-operation.keep: keep independent redistricting on the books

us-policy-positions:government-operation.against: keep photo ID to vote off the books

without.for: A voter doesn't have to show a photo ID at the polls, so nobody checks who is casting the ballot.
without.against: A voter can be turned away from the polls for lacking the right card.

with.for: A voter shows a photo ID at the polls, the same as boarding a plane.
with.against: A voter has to show a photo ID, and some folks without one are turned away.

us-policy-positions:government-operation.keep: keep photo ID to vote on the books

us-policy-positions:government-operation.to: let people register and vote on the same day
us-policy-positions:government-operation.for: let people register and vote on the same day
us-policy-positions:government-operation.against: keep same-day voter registration off the books

without.for: A citizen who misses the registration deadline can't vote that year.
without.against: A voter signs up ahead of time, so the rolls can be checked before Election Day.

with.for: A citizen can register and vote on the same day.
with.against: People can sign up and vote on the same day, before anyone checks the rolls.

us-policy-positions:government-operation.keep: keep same-day voter registration on the books

us-policy-positions:government-operation.about: a ban on lobbying after leaving office
us-policy-positions:government-operation.against: keep a ban on lobbying after leaving office off the books

without.for: An official can leave office on Friday and lobby their old colleagues on Monday.
without.against: A former official can go to work wherever they please.

with.for: A former official has to wait before lobbying their old colleagues.
with.against: The law tells a former official where they can work.

us-policy-positions:government-operation.repeal: repeal a ban on lobbying after leaving office
us-policy-positions:government-operation.keep: keep a ban on lobbying after leaving office on the books

us-policy-positions:government-operation.against: keep more local government power off the books

without.for: A town has to ask the state's permission for most of what it wants to do.
without.against: The state sets one set of rules, so a business or a family knows what to expect from town to town.

with.for: Towns can do more without asking the state first.
with.against: Every town makes its own rules, and they change from one town line to the next.

us-policy-positions:government-operation.keep: keep more local government power on the books

us-policy-positions:government-operation.to: limit how long legislators can serve
us-policy-positions:government-operation.for: limit how long legislators can serve
us-policy-positions:government-operation.against: keep term limits for legislators off the books

without.for: A legislator can serve for as long as they keep winning.
without.against: The voters decide how long a legislator serves, every election.

with.for: The law limits how long a legislator can serve.
with.against: The law throws out a legislator the voters want to keep.

us-policy-positions:government-operation.keep: keep term limits for legislators on the books

us-policy-positions:civil-family-communi.about: a ban on discrimination in housing and work
us-policy-positions:civil-family-communi.to: ban discrimination in housing and at work
us-policy-positions:civil-family-communi.for: ban discrimination in housing and at work
us-policy-positions:civil-family-communi.against: keep a ban on discrimination in housing and work off the books

without.for: A person can be turned away from a job or an apartment for who they are.
without.against: A small business owner or a landlord can run things by their own conscience.

with.for: Nobody can be turned away from a job or an apartment for who they are.
with.against: A small business owner can be taken to court for running things by their own conscience.

us-policy-positions:civil-family-communi.repeal: repeal a ban on discrimination in housing and work
us-policy-positions:civil-family-communi.keep: keep a ban on discrimination in housing and work on the books

us-policy-positions:civil-family-communi.against: keep dedicated funding for parks off the books

without.for: The parks get whatever is left at the end of the budget.
without.against: The parks compete for money every year with everything else.

with.for: The parks have money set aside for them every year.
with.against: The parks get their money first, whatever else needs it.

us-policy-positions:civil-family-communi.keep: keep dedicated funding for parks on the books

us-policy-positions:civil-family-communi.against: keep restricting abortion off the books

without.for: Abortion is legal here, through much of a pregnancy.
without.against: A woman makes her own decision about a pregnancy, with her doctor.

with.for: The law protects an unborn child here.
with.against: The law makes the decision about a pregnancy for a woman and her doctor.

us-policy-positions:civil-family-communi.keep: keep restricting abortion on the books

us-policy-positions:technology-privacy.a.to: require age checks for social media accounts
us-policy-positions:technology-privacy.a.for: require age checks for social media accounts
us-policy-positions:technology-privacy.a.against: keep age checks for social media off the books

without.for: A child can open a social media account in a minute with no one checking their age.
without.against: Parents decide what their children do online, and adults don't have to hand over an ID to use a website.

with.for: Social media sites have to check a user's age.
with.against: Every adult has to hand an ID to a website before they can post.

us-policy-positions:technology-privacy.a.repeal: repeal age checks for social media
us-policy-positions:technology-privacy.a.keep: keep age checks for social media on the books

us-policy-positions:technology-privacy.r.to: limit how government uses facial recognition
us-policy-positions:technology-privacy.r.for: limit how government uses facial recognition
us-policy-positions:technology-privacy.r.against: keep limits on government facial recognition off the books

without.for: Government agencies can scan a face in a crowd with no rules at all.
without.against: Police can use facial recognition to find a suspect fast.

with.for: The law limits how government uses facial recognition.
with.against: The law keeps police from using a tool that finds suspects fast.

us-policy-positions:technology-privacy.r.repeal: repeal limits on government facial recognition
us-policy-positions:technology-privacy.r.keep: keep limits on government facial recognition on the books

us-policy-positions:technology-privacy.c.against: keep a consumer data privacy law off the books

without.for: A company can sell what it knows about you without asking.
without.against: A company and its customers set the terms between them.

with.for: A company has to protect what it knows about you.
with.against: Every business, down to the corner shop, has paperwork to do over the data it keeps.

us-policy-positions:technology-privacy.c.repeal: repeal a consumer data privacy law
us-policy-positions:technology-privacy.c.keep: keep a consumer data privacy law on the books

us-policy-positions:agriculture-natural-.to: limit how much groundwater can be pumped
us-policy-positions:agriculture-natural-.for: limit how much groundwater can be pumped
us-policy-positions:agriculture-natural-.against: keep limits on pumping groundwater off the books

without.for: Anyone with a well can pump as much groundwater as they like, and the wells are dropping.
without.against: A landowner can pump water from their own well.

with.for: The law limits how much groundwater can be pumped, so the wells don't run dry.
with.against: The law tells a farmer how much water they can pump from their own well.

us-policy-positions:agriculture-natural-.keep: keep limits on pumping groundwater on the books

us-policy-positions:agriculture-natural-.against: keep protecting farmland from development off the books

without.for: Good farmland can be paved over for the next subdivision.
without.against: A farmer can sell their land to whoever they choose.

with.for: Farmland is protected from being paved over.
with.against: A farmer can't sell their own land to the buyer who offers the most.

us-policy-positions:agriculture-natural-.keep: keep protecting farmland from development on the books

us-federal-positions:budget.pay-for-a-hi.about: raising the debt limit only with spending cuts to match
us-federal-positions:budget.pay-for-a-hi.to: raise the debt limit only with spending cuts to match
us-federal-positions:budget.pay-for-a-hi.for: raise the debt limit only with spending cuts to match
us-federal-positions:budget.pay-for-a-hi.against: keep raising the debt limit only with spending cuts to match off the books

without.for: The debt limit can be raised without cutting a dollar of spending to match.
without.against: The debt limit is raised so this country pays the bills it already owes.

with.for: Any rise in the debt limit has to come with spending cuts to match.
with.against: Paying bills we already owe now comes with cuts to programs people count on.

us-federal-positions:budget.pay-for-a-hi.repeal: repeal raising the debt limit only with spending cuts to match
us-federal-positions:budget.pay-for-a-hi.keep: keep raising the debt limit only with spending cuts to match on the books

us-federal-positions:tax.raise-top-incom.about: a higher top income tax rate
us-federal-positions:tax.raise-top-incom.to: raise the top income tax rate
us-federal-positions:tax.raise-top-incom.for: raise the top income tax rate
us-federal-positions:tax.raise-top-incom.against: keep a higher top income tax rate off the books

without.for: The top income tax rate is lower than it was a generation ago.
without.against: The top income tax rate leaves money with the people who start businesses and hire.

with.for: The top income tax rate is higher than it was.
with.against: The top income tax rate is higher than it was, and the people who start businesses keep less.

us-federal-positions:tax.raise-top-incom.repeal: repeal a higher top income tax rate
us-federal-positions:tax.raise-top-incom.keep: keep a higher top income tax rate on the books

us-federal-positions:monetary-financial..about: a cap on consumer loan interest
us-federal-positions:monetary-financial..to: cap the interest on consumer loans
us-federal-positions:monetary-financial..for: cap the interest on consumer loans
us-federal-positions:monetary-financial..against: keep a cap on consumer loan interest off the books

without.for: There is no national cap on the interest a lender can charge.
without.against: A family that needs cash fast can still find a lender willing to make the loan.

with.for: A national cap limits the interest on a consumer loan.
with.against: A national cap limits loan interest, and families with poor credit can't find anyone who will lend to them.

us-federal-positions:monetary-financial..repeal: repeal a cap on consumer loan interest
us-federal-positions:monetary-financial..keep: keep a cap on consumer loan interest on the books

us-federal-positions:defense.grow-defens.against: keep more defense spending off the books

without.for: Our defense budget is not keeping up with the threats we face.
without.against: We already spend more on defense than the next several countries together.

with.for: We spend more on defense than we did.
with.against: We spend more on defense than we did, while needs at home wait.

us-federal-positions:defense.grow-defens.keep: keep more defense spending on the books

us-federal-positions:foreign-affairs.inc.against: keep more foreign aid off the books

without.for: Foreign aid is less than one penny of every federal dollar.
without.against: We send money abroad while families here go without.

with.for: We give more in foreign aid than we did, and our friends abroad know we're with them.
with.against: We send more money abroad than we did, while families here go without.

us-federal-positions:foreign-affairs.inc.keep: keep more foreign aid on the books

us-federal-positions:trade.raise-tariffs.against: keep higher tariffs off the books

without.for: Most goods come into this country with little or no tariff, and our factories pay for it.
without.against: Most goods come into this country with little or no tariff, and that keeps prices down.

with.for: Goods from abroad carry higher tariffs, and our factories have a fair shot.
with.against: Goods from abroad carry higher tariffs, and families pay more for them.

us-federal-positions:trade.raise-tariffs.keep: keep higher tariffs on the books

us-federal-positions:immigration.admit-m.against: keep admitting more immigrants off the books

without.for: People wait years, sometimes decades, to come here legally.
without.against: We set a limit on how many people come here each year, and we enforce it.

with.for: More people can come here legally each year.
with.against: More people come here each year than we can take in.

us-federal-positions:immigration.admit-m.keep: keep admitting more immigrants on the books

us-federal-positions:health.medicare-dru.against: keep Medicare negotiating drug prices off the books

without.for: Medicare pays whatever the drug companies ask for most medicines.
without.against: The companies that make new medicines set their prices, and that money pays for the next cure.

with.for: Medicare bargains with the drug companies over what it pays.
with.against: Washington sets what the drug companies get paid, and fewer new medicines are on the way.

us-federal-positions:health.medicare-dru.keep: keep Medicare negotiating drug prices on the books

us-federal-positions:social-insurance.ra.against: keep a higher retirement age off the books

without.for: Full Social Security starts at sixty-seven, while the fund that pays it runs short.
without.against: Full Social Security starts at sixty-seven, the age people have worked toward.

with.for: Full Social Security starts later than it did, and the fund lasts longer.
with.against: Folks have to work longer than they planned before full Social Security starts.

us-federal-positions:social-insurance.ra.keep: keep a higher retirement age on the books

us-federal-positions:education.forgive-s.against: keep forgiving student loans off the books

without.for: A young person can leave school owing more than their parents paid for a house.
without.against: Folks who borrow for school pay back what they borrowed, the same as any other loan.

with.for: Much of what students borrowed has been forgiven.
with.against: Folks who never went to college, or who paid their loans off, are paying for other people's loans.

us-federal-positions:education.forgive-s.keep: keep forgiving student loans on the books

us-federal-positions:housing.vouchers-fo.about: housing vouchers for every family that qualifies
us-federal-positions:housing.vouchers-fo.to: give a housing voucher to every family that qualifies
us-federal-positions:housing.vouchers-fo.for: give a housing voucher to every family that qualifies
us-federal-positions:housing.vouchers-fo.against: keep housing vouchers for every family that qualifies off the books

without.for: Most families who qualify for housing help sit on a waiting list for years.
without.against: Housing help goes as far as the money we set aside for it.

with.for: Every family that qualifies gets a housing voucher.
with.against: Every family that qualifies gets a voucher, and the bill grows every year.

us-federal-positions:housing.vouchers-fo.repeal: repeal housing vouchers for every family that qualifies
us-federal-positions:housing.vouchers-fo.keep: keep housing vouchers for every family that qualifies on the books

us-federal-positions:transport-water.exp.against: keep more passenger rail off the books

without.for: A train is not a real choice for most trips in this country.
without.against: Most people get where they're going by car, and the roads are what they need.

with.for: More of the country can travel by train.
with.against: More of the country's travel money goes to trains few people ride.

us-federal-positions:transport-water.exp.keep: keep more passenger rail on the books

us-federal-positions:energy-environment..against: keep limits on power plant carbon off the books

without.for: Power plants can put as much carbon into the air as they like.
without.against: Power plants run on whatever keeps the lights on at the lowest price.

with.for: Power plants are limited in how much carbon they put into the air.
with.against: Power plants run under limits that close the ones that keep power cheap.

us-federal-positions:energy-environment..repeal: repeal limits on power plant carbon
us-federal-positions:energy-environment..keep: keep limits on power plant carbon on the books

us-federal-positions:agriculture.cut-far.against: keep cutting farm subsidies off the books

without.for: The biggest farms collect the biggest checks from Washington.
without.against: Farm support helps a family farm get through a bad year.

with.for: Farm subsidies are smaller than they were.
with.against: Farm support is smaller than it was, and a bad year can cost a family its farm.

us-federal-positions:agriculture.cut-far.keep: keep cutting farm subsidies on the books

us-federal-positions:emergencies.states-.to: have the states share more of disaster costs
us-federal-positions:emergencies.states-.for: have the states share more of disaster costs
us-federal-positions:emergencies.states-.against: keep states sharing disaster costs off the books

without.against: Washington helps pay when a disaster hits, so no state is left to rebuild alone.

with.for: The states pay a larger share of what a disaster costs.
with.against: A state hit by a disaster is left with more of the bill.

us-federal-positions:emergencies.states-.keep: keep states sharing disaster costs on the books

us-federal-positions:justice-rights.redu.against: keep shorter mandatory minimum sentences off the books

without.for: A judge has to hand down the same long sentence no matter the case.
without.against: A serious crime carries a set sentence, the same in every courtroom.

with.for: Judges have more room to fit a sentence to the case.
with.against: Serious crimes can bring shorter sentences, depending on the judge.

us-federal-positions:justice-rights.redu.keep: keep shorter mandatory minimum sentences on the books

us-federal-positions:government.ban-cong.about: a ban on stock trading by members of Congress
us-federal-positions:government.ban-cong.to: ban members of Congress from trading stocks
us-federal-positions:government.ban-cong.for: ban members of Congress from trading stocks
us-federal-positions:government.ban-cong.against: keep a ban on stock trading by members of Congress off the books

without.for: A lawmaker in Washington can buy and sell stock in the very companies they write laws for.
without.against: Members of Congress report every trade they make, and the voters can see them.

with.for: Lawmakers in Washington can't trade stocks.
with.against: Members of Congress can't own the same stocks every other American can.

us-federal-positions:government.ban-cong.repeal: repeal a ban on stock trading by members of Congress
us-federal-positions:government.ban-cong.keep: keep a ban on stock trading by members of Congress on the books

us-federal-positions:science-communicati.to: pass a national data privacy law
us-federal-positions:science-communicati.for: pass a national data privacy law
us-federal-positions:science-communicati.against: keep a national data privacy law off the books

without.for: There is no national law that protects your personal data.
without.against: Each state writes its own rules about personal data.

with.for: A national law protects your personal data.
with.against: A national law decides how every business handles data, down to the smallest shop.

us-federal-positions:science-communicati.repeal: repeal a national data privacy law
us-federal-positions:science-communicati.keep: keep a national data privacy law on the books

us-federal-positions:territories-culture.for: make the nation's capital a state
us-federal-positions:territories-culture.against: keep statehood for the nation's capital off the books

without.for: The people who live in the nation's capital pay federal taxes and have no voting member in the House or the Senate.
without.against: The nation's capital belongs to the whole country, not to any one state.

with.for: The nation's capital is a state, with a vote in the House and the Senate.
